title: Top cost drivers visualization: ranking, deltas, and explainability copy
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
Context
Usage Insights needs a “Top cost drivers” module that helps engineers + FinOps quickly answer:
1) Where is spend coming from? (ranking)
2) What changed vs last period? (deltas)
3) Why did it change? (explainable drivers, not opaque scores)

This ticket covers design explorations for: ranking layout, delta presentation (WoW / previous period), tooltips + definitions, and explainability copy that is accurate and non-misleading given known attribution caveats (retries/fallbacks/streaming/cache).

Links / references
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/in-console-usage-insights-prd.json
- Console UX spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/usage-insights-console-ux-spec.json
- Brainstorm heuristics: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/console-and-tooling/top-cost-drivers-heuristics-brainstorm.json
- Freshness indicators: ENG-3824 (UI banner + timestamps)
- Slack design review thread: sources/slack/design/1738094402.json

User problems (from research + customer calls)
- “My invoice is up 30%—what endpoint caused it?”
- “Did token out go up, or did we switch models?”
- “We turned on streaming—did that change cost?”
- “Cache hit rate dropped, but which route is impacted?”
- “Finance wants a weekly explanation, not just a number.”

Design goals
- Make it skimmable in <30 seconds (top 3–5 drivers).
- Make it drillable (one click to filtered breakdown table).
- Make it defensible (explain what the system observed and what it did NOT infer).
- Avoid false precision (don’t imply causal certainty; clearly label comparisons and partial data).

Non-goals
- Not designing auto-optimization actions (we can link to docs/levers).
- Not designing export flow (covered in DES-914), but ensure module doesn’t conflict with export/share affordances.

Exploration summary
Option A: “Driver cards” (recommended)
- Horizontal row (or 2-column grid) of up to 5 cards.
- Each card has: Driver title, quantified delta, primary dimension, and a ‘View details’ link.
- Example cards:
  1) Token out ↑ +35% (Route: /v1/chat/completions, Model: llama-3.1-70b)
  2) Cache hit rate ↓ -12 pts (Route: /v1/embeddings, Model: text-embed-3-large)
  3) Retries ↑ +0.8% (Region: us-east-1, Route: /v1/chat/completions)
  4) Fallbacks ↑ +2.1% (Primary model saturated → fallback model engaged)
  5) Context length ↑ P95 +1.2k tokens (driving higher input tokens)

Why Option A
- Supports multiple driver types without forcing a single stacked chart grammar.
- Works well with empty/partial data and with varying explanation length.
- Keeps “explainability” close to the quantified metric.

Option B: “Leaderboard table” (secondary)
- Table with Rank / Driver / Change / Impact / Scope.
- More scalable but reads like analytics; less approachable for FinOps and more likely to be misread as causation.

Option C: “Waterfall” (rejected for beta)
- Visually attractive but implies additive decomposition of total cost. Our heuristics are not guaranteed to be additive and could double-count correlated factors (token out and model mix shifts). Too risky for early beta.

Ranking & scoring guidance
- We should not show a single hidden “score.” Prefer explicit ranking by estimated cost impact when available; otherwise rank by magnitude of change and show “Impact unavailable” label.
- Recommended rank logic for UI text (not prescribing backend): “Ranked by estimated cost impact (when available), otherwise by magnitude of change.”

Delta presentation
- Default comparison: previous period of equal length (e.g., last 7d vs prior 7d).
- Each card shows: % change + absolute delta where meaningful.
  - For spend metrics: “+$1,240 (+18%)”
  - For rates: “-12.0 pts (from 58% → 46%)”
  - For distributions: “P95 +1.2k tokens (from 3.4k → 4.6k)”
- Include a small “Compared to: Previous period” label beneath module title (global, not per card).
- If time range < 24h, switch label to “Compared to: Previous equal window” to avoid implying WoW.

Tooltips & definitions (copy draft)
We need consistent, short definitions that match telemetry semantics and avoid implying causality.

Module title tooltip
- “Top cost drivers highlight the largest changes in usage patterns that correlate with higher spend. They are indicators, not a full accounting decomposition.”

Card template copy
- Header: Driver name (e.g., “Token out increased”)
- Body (1–2 lines): “Output tokens increased on /v1/chat/completions (llama-3.1-70b), increasing cost vs the previous period.”
- Secondary line: “View breakdown” → deep link to filtered table.

Metric tooltips (initial set)
- Output tokens: “Tokens generated by the model in responses (including streamed chunks). More output tokens typically increases cost.”
- Input tokens: “Tokens in prompts and system/context. Longer context increases cost and can increase latency.”
- Cache hit rate: “Share of requests served using prefix/KV cache for eligible routes/models. A lower hit rate increases compute per request.”
- Retries: “Requests that were re-attempted due to transient errors/timeouts. Retries may increase billed usage depending on when failure occurs.”
- Fallbacks: “Requests served by an alternate model due to policy or capacity constraints. Costs may differ from the requested model.”
- Streaming overhead: “Additional work associated with streaming responses (e.g., longer-lived connections). Impact varies by route and traffic patterns.”

Guardrails & warnings
- Freshness / partial data: If telemetry lag exceeds threshold (from ENG-3824), show module-level warning:
  - Banner: “Some data is still processing. Changes may be understated.”
- Low sample size: If request count is below threshold, show subtle label on affected cards:
  - “Low volume—trend may be noisy”
- Attribution caveat: For retry-related drivers, include inline “Learn more” to docs troubleshooting section.

Drill-down behavior
- Clicking a card navigates to route/model breakdown table with filters pre-applied:
  - Time range same as module
  - Dimension filters based on card scope (route, model, region, deployment mode)
  - Adds a “Compared to” toggle surfaced in table header (existing spec) to verify delta.

Empty states
- No drivers (no meaningful change):
  - “No significant changes detected for this period.”
  - Secondary: “Try expanding the time range.”
- Missing required dimensions (e.g., route tags absent):
  - “Top drivers unavailable because route attribution is incomplete for this workspace.”
  - CTA: “View data quality” (links to freshness/quality panel once available) + docs.

Accessibility notes
- Card grid must be keyboard navigable; card link has visible focus state.
- Delta colors must meet contrast; do not rely on red/green only.
- Use icons sparingly; ensure screen reader labels for “increase/decrease.”

Open questions for Eng/PM
1) Do we have reliable “estimated cost impact” per driver type for beta (ENG-3819), or should we avoid “impact” entirely and show only deltas?
2) Do we want to show “Top drivers” scoped to current filters only, or allow a ‘Global’ mode that ignores route/model filters? (Recommendation: respect current filters to reduce surprise.)
3) How do we label fallbacks: show requested model vs served model, or only “served by fallback”? (Recommend both in tooltip: “Requested X → Served Y”.)
4) Should streaming overhead be a driver in beta, given metric ambiguity? (PM to confirm.)

Deliverables in this ticket
- Final recommended module layout (Option A) with mobile behavior notes.
- Copy set: module tooltip + driver card templates + metric tooltips.
- States: partial data, low volume, empty.
- Handoff notes for implementation (spacing, truncation rules, max lines).

Acceptance criteria
- PM (Marissa/Paula) signs off on wording that avoids causal claims and matches known constraints.
- Eng (Dylan/Chloe) confirms drill-down mapping is implementable with planned filters.
- Design review resolves clutter concern from Slack thread (limit to 5 cards + “View all drivers” optional link).

Notes for handoff
- Max 5 cards by default; if more, show “View all” linking to a dedicated drivers list (phase 2).
- Card body truncation: 2 lines max; tooltip for full text.
- Number formatting: use billing currency settings; for rates, show points + from/to when available.
comments: 2026-02-07 (Alicia Perez): Started exploration in Figma: card vs leaderboard vs waterfall. Initial take: cards are more approachable; waterfall risky because heuristics aren’t additive.

2026-02-10 (George Mbatha): From quick feedback sessions: users want the card to explicitly name the scope (route/model) and they strongly prefer seeing “from → to” values for rates (cache hit) instead of only % change.

2026-02-12 (Dylan Brooks): Implementation note: we can deep link to breakdown table with route/model filters easily. For ‘impact’ we may only have approximate cost deltas for token changes in beta; retries/fallbacks may be v2.
2026-02-14 (Marissa Cole): Please avoid phrasing like “caused by” or “due to” unless we can prove causality. Suggest: “correlates with higher spend” + “indicator” language in tooltip.
2026-02-18 (Allison Grant): Data caveat: freshness lag can be >2h during backfills/late events. Need a module-level partial-data message; don’t bury it in a tooltip.

2026-02-21 (Tessa Morgan): Design review: approved direction on cards + strict limit of 5. Open: whether we show an overall comparison selector near title or rely on global time range + ‘previous period’ assumption.

2026-02-26 (Chloe Martin): Backend will return a list of driver objects with type + scope fields + delta fields. Please keep UI copy flexible by driver type; we can provide short explainability strings from service, but UX should still have canonical tooltips/definitions.

2026-02-28 (Alicia Perez): Updated copy to remove causal verbs; added ‘Compared to previous period’ label and low-volume badge. Ready for PM copy sign-off + Eng feasibility check on showing from/to values.
